summary: At command step 19, JavaScript preflight refuses a selected boulder before pickup_object runs. C reaches lift_object and carry_count; for one non-gold object whose weight reaches max_capacity, carry_count reports that it cannot be lifted and returns zero, so pickup ends normally with the object still on the floor. Port that complete message branch and bypass preflight only when one ordinary quantity-one object is certainly unliftable. Automatic random-arrival projection must continue to treat that object as remaining on the floor.

source.branch: For an ordinary non-gold object with count 1, when max_capacity() + obj->owt >= 0, the preliminary weight check does not return count; the single-object branch sets qq to 0, emits the cannot-lift message, and returns 0. The selected boulder is not in Sokoban, is not a loadstone, and the hero is not a giant, so lift_object reaches carry_count.

pickup.c:lift_object calls carry_count and consumes its returned count
pickup.c:pickup_object scare-scroll branch calls carry_count directly

JavaScript js/pickup.js:preflightPickupObjects currently rejects when inv_weight(state)+addedWeight >= 2*weight_cap(state), before the source-ordered pickup_object call. For a sole ordinary quantity-one object this is equivalent to carry_count’s no-lift preliminary condition, but source behavior is to let pickup_object reach carry_count, print the message, and return normally. Automatic floor-pickup planning also uses this preflight, so its remaining-object projection must retain the unliftable object for check_here.
